metric.metric: Stranded power and space per cabinet
metric.definition: Utility power or floor space that is allocated and paid for but cannot be used, because the other of the pair ran out first or airflow limits were reached.

reading.body:
Stranded power and space per cabinet measures utility power or floor space that has been allocated and paid for but cannot actually be used, because the other half of the pair, power or space, ran out first or airflow limits were reached.

A data hall can be full by power and half empty by floor space, or the reverse, and tracking both dimensions per cabinet is described as how operators find capacity they already own before spending money to build more. That framing turns this into an efficiency-of-existing-assets metric rather than a capacity-planning one, relevant to any operator trying to understand whether their real constraint is more power, more floor space, or better provisioning of what they already have.

Its siblings, server utilization rate and floor loading limits, are grouped under Capacity and server use, together addressing how much of a facility's provisioned resources actually get used productively.
